name: SOLV Energy

ownership.notes: IPO'd Feb 11-12, 2026 at $25/share (~$589M gross with greenshoe; ~$5-6B reported valuation) — the first pure-play US solar+storage EPC to list. PE firm American Securities (which bought the business from Swinerton in Dec 2021 for a reported ~$2B) remained majority holder post-IPO and sold down in a May 2026 secondary at $36.

summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: SOLV Energy is the pure-play benchmark of the US solar+storage EPC tier — >21 GWdc built across 500+ plants since its 2008 Swinerton Renewable Energy origins, the #2 US BESS builder of 2024 (4,586 MWh installed, a 35x ramp from 2022), an ~8.5 GW ERCOT construction record, and the industry's largest solar O&M fleet (~22 GWdc across ~155 plants). Its February 2026 Nasdaq IPO (MWH) and $8.9B backlog (~100% safe-harbored, storage-linked slice $2.5B and climbing) make it the cleanest public read on the storage-EPC cycle. The channel fact that matters most: on every verified flagship BESS build (Arevon's Vikings and Eland, Intersect's Oberon), the batteries were owner-furnished Tesla Megapacks — SOLV installs what owners buy — so its battery-selection influence concentrates in mid-size utility/co-op jobs, its advertised battery-module procurement scope, and the augmentation cycle of the O&M fleet, where OEM lock-in is weakest. It is 'actively exploring storage for data centers' (Q2 2026) and just bought Roberson Waite for urban BESS + substation capability.
ecosystemRole: We assess SOLV as a constructability gatekeeper and services annuity rather than a procurement principal: winning SOLV means install-compatibility, commissioning familiarity, and a voice in owner equipment selection (its CEO explicitly markets lifecycle-data-driven 'select equipment' influence), not purchase orders. For the relationship web it is the physical link between Batch B's buyers and Batch A's suppliers — it built Arevon's Tesla flagships, services Intersect Power (Google's co-location partner) and SB Energy (the Stargate-linked developer) under O&M, and its Sungrow experience is inverter-side only. Its 22 GW O&M fleet is the quiet strategic asset for any battery OEM: augmentation and repowering purchases recur for decades and are less FEOC-visible than new-build ITC procurement.

productsAndServices.name: Utility-scale solar + storage EPC
productsAndServices.description: >21 GWdc built across 500+ plants; 50+ BESS projects in 14 states; 2024 BESS installs 4,586 MWh (#2 nationally per Solar Power World). Verified flagship builds: Vikings (Arevon — 157 MWdc + 150 MW/600 MWh Tesla Megapack, COD Nov 2024, 'first US utility-scale solar peaker'); Eland 1 & 2 (Arevon — 758 MWdc + 1,200 MWh combined, Tesla Megapack 2 XL, >$2B complex); Oberon 1 (Intersect Power — 339 MWdc scope + 500 kV substation/gen-tie + 250 MWac/1,000 MWh Tesla BESS); Chirreon (Torch/Trico co-op — 13 MW PV + 15 MW/2-hr BESS). Active slate (Jun 2026): >4 GWdc of 600+ MW projects including a 1,200 MWdc Arizona solar+BESS — the largest single award in company history (owners undisclosed).
productsAndServices.positioning: #2 solar contractor per ENR (No. 66 Top 400 overall); top-5 by installed volume in Solar Power World's 2025-2026 lists; ~8.5 GW built in ERCOT. Rival Rosendin takes Arevon's standalone BESS (Condor, Peregrine, Nighthawk) while SOLV wins the hybrids — the split to watch in its home market.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: EPC contracts with LNTP structures (customers prepay deposits for long-lead equipment); repeat owners include Arevon, Intersect Power, Matrix Renewables, Sol Systems, SB Energy, Clēnera; union labor capability demonstrated (250+ union workers at Vikings).
productsAndServices.targetSegments: IPPs, utilities, co-ops, CCA-contracted developers — CAISO and ERCOT-centric with national reach (41 states licensed).
productsAndServices.roadmap: FY2026 revenue guided to $3.87-3.97B; 'majority of projects are solar plus storage now' (Q2 2026 call).

productsAndServices.name: O&M / services platform (the annuity — and the OEM entry point)
productsAndServices.description: ~22 GWdc / ~155 plants under long-term O&M (+4.8 GW added in the year to Apr 2025), 140+ sites remote-monitored from the San Diego Operations Center. Services include BESS testing/repair/upgrades, NETA-compliant high-voltage work, and battery augmentation and repowering. Named O&M customers: Intersect Power, SB Energy (longstanding), Greenalia, Matrix Renewables (new 2025).
productsAndServices.positioning: The largest independent solar O&M fleet in the US — a recurring counterparty for augmentation-stage battery procurement where owner lock-in to the original OEM is weakest.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Long-term O&M contracts, often bundled with EPC wins.
productsAndServices.roadmap: BESS/substation services expansion is the stated growth vector; augmentation demand compounds as the 2020-2023 build cohort ages.

productsAndServices.name: Self-perform + adjacency acquisitions
productsAndServices.description: Self-perform field model (~1,219 field employees; large apprenticeship program — 1,219 apprentices/students in development, DOL ACE Network participant). Acquisitions: Sacramento Drilling (early 2025 — foundations self-perform), Spartan Infrastructure (Jun 2025 — high-voltage T&D), Roberson Waite Electric (~$45M, closed Jul 2026 — Anaheim substation/testing contractor adding urban BESS + regulated-utility capability, press-linked to data-center-supporting infrastructure).
productsAndServices.positioning: Vertical integration of the scopes that bottleneck storage builds: foundations, HV interconnection, substations.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Its own project execution plus regulated-utility work (Roberson Waite).
productsAndServices.roadmap: 'Actively exploring storage for data centers' as a growth avenue (Q2 2026 call) — the AIDC on-ramp is urban BESS + substation scope, not data-center buildings.

recentDevelopments.read: The template build: owner-furnished Tesla, union labor, Buy-America framing — the domestic-content EPC playbook in one project.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess SOLV as a constructability and services channel, not a procurement principal: every verified flagship BESS was owner-furnished Tesla, and its influence runs through equipment-selection advice, install-compatibility standards, and commissioning familiarity. A battery OEM 'wins' SOLV by being easy to build and service, which then lowers friction in owner selections — not by selling it containers.

(High confidence) We assess the O&M fleet (~22 GW, ~155 plants, augmentation/repowering in scope) as the most underrated Hithium-relevant surface in the EPC tier: augmentation purchases recur for decades, are less FEOC-visible than new-build ITC procurement, and the incumbent-OEM lock weakens as fleets age. SOLV is the counterparty that executes those purchases.

(Moderate confidence) We assess SOLV's public posture as domestic-leaning but not China-hostile: CEO Hershman's record is anti-tariff yet pro-domestic-manufacturing (past SEIA board chair), the backlog is marketed as 100% safe-harbored and tax-credit-clean, and Vikings was sold on American-made components. As a newly public company it has no appetite to champion a §154-named supplier — but no blanket aversion either (Sungrow inverters run its flagship).

(Moderate confidence) We assess the AIDC angle as forming, not formed: 'actively exploring storage for data centers,' the Roberson Waite urban-BESS/substation capability, and O&M relationships with Stargate-linked SB Energy and Google-partnered Intersect Power put SOLV one contract away from AIDC-adjacent storage construction — worth monitoring for the first named award.

(Moderate confidence) For the Hithium lens: treat SOLV as an install-ecosystem qualification target — container handling specs, foundation/spacing standards, commissioning interfaces, service training — so that when an owner (a KCE, a Plus Power, a post-2029 Terra-Gen) considers Hithium hardware, the largest storage-experienced EPC bench in CAISO/ERCOT is already familiar with it rather than pricing in first-build risk.
